newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran cleric urges Moslem states to sever U.S. ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric urges Moslem states to sever U.S. ties.

text.p: A leading Iranian cleric on Friday urged Moslem states to sever ties with Washington over a U.S. House of Representatives vote to reaffirm that Jerusalem must become Israel's undivided capital, Iran's IRNA news agency said.

"Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati here today (Friday) addressed himself to Muslim governments calling on them to sever relations with Washington in protest against U.S. support for the decision to declare al-Quds (Jerusalem) the capital of the Zionist regime," IRNA said.
Jannati, a senior member of Iran's powerful Guardian Council, made the appeal in front of thousands of worshippers during a sermon at Tehran University, IRNA said.
"Washington and the Zionist regime do not seem to be the least concerned about the feelings of the Muslim nations in that respect," IRNA quoted Jannati as saying.
The Guardian Council is a body of clerics and lawyers which has the power to reject legislation passed by the country's parliament. The council also screens candidates and oversees elections.
